Also raises the input size cap so headers can reach MAX_HEADERS_SIZE, and checks that splitting the same byte stream differently never changes the parsed result.

why: P3 because it adds real coverage of previously unreachable parser resume paths (header, chunk, body) in a security-relevant HTTP parsing component, confirmed by reviewer testing that the new assertions catch mutations there.
It does not fix an active flake or unblock other work, so it ranks as solid, worthwhile coverage rather than urgent.

result.summary: This PR extends the http_request fuzz target to exercise the resumable-parse paths of HTTPRequest's state machine, which the prior single-pass target could not reach. It feeds the same input through a mock client both whole and sliced into arbitrary pieces, asserting the two runs produce identical parsed requests, since HTTP framing must not depend on how the byte stream was split by the network. It also raises the fuzz input cap so generated inputs can reach MAX_HEADERS_SIZE (8192 bytes), previously unreachable because the cap sat at 4096.
result.problem: The existing http_request fuzz harness parsed each input in a single pass, so the code paths that resume a partially-read request (across header, chunk, and body boundaries) were never exercised, leaving that logic essentially untested by fuzzing despite being new, security-relevant surface added in #35735.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp noted several parser paths (header resume, chunk resume, body resume, chunked Transfer-Encoding branch) are not reached by the current qa-assets corpus; a corpus/dictionary follow-up (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#293) was opened separately to address this, deliberately kept out of this PR due to lint rules.
hodlinator noted corecheck.dev shows no significant coverage difference yet, attributed to the corpus not being updated, not a flaw in the PR itself.
resolved_concerns: hodlinator's naming/style suggestions (Receive/ReceiveBytesFromSocket, ZeroSock usage, string_view slicing, comment wording) were all taken by the author.
fanquake's CI build failure (Sock::operator= hidden warning) was fixed by switching to ZeroSock.

result.card: This PR extends the http_request fuzz harness to exercise HTTPRequest's resumable parsing paths (header, chunk, body resumption across I/O cycles) by feeding identical input both whole and sliced, asserting framing must not depend on stream segmentation, and raises the fuzz input cap so headers can reach MAX_HEADERS_SIZE. It closes a real coverage gap: previously the target parsed each input in one pass so partial-read resume logic added in #35735 was fuzz-unreachable. Two reviewers (jeanpablojp, hodlinator) independently rebuilt with ASan/UBSan, replayed the qa-assets corpus, and confirmed the new assertions catch mutations on the resume paths, giving it Strong agreement. All prior CI failures and style nits were resolved through iteration, leaving the PR Ready for review. A related follow-up to actually update the qa-assets corpus/dictionary to reach some of the newly-tested branches was deliberately split into a separate PR (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#293).
